matches.quote: The authors should reconcile the fluence scales, and if the data come from different beamtimes, say so and give the spot size and absorbed fluence for each.
The explanation that the RDS signal falls at high fluence "because the RXD intensity reduction is larger at temperatures closer to the AFM transition temperature" is hard to follow
The only direct argument against a profile change, that "the RXD peak width remains nearly constant" (p. 4, Fig. 2C), is weak: the peak top is saturated
RXD and RDS recover with τ ≈ 7 ns (Fig. 4D), which the paper attributes to an intrinsic magnon–phonon bottleneck limited by dispersion mismatch. A simpler alternative is untested
The authors should mark which statements are measured and which modelled, reword the abstract accordingly, and move the cross-material and design statements to an outlook
The tr-NRDS was taken at ESRF with ~100 ps pulses... a picosecond (800 nm-derived) pump... excitation densities and fluence calibrations are not matched.
Fig. 2E states the RDS energy scan was taken at (½, −0.08, −½), where Fig. 3F shows A_RDS close to zero; confirm the momentum and explain the choice.
Long-lived photocarriers are excluded only by citing other cuprates... The authors should measure transient optical reflectivity or absorption on the same crystal
the ~500 K hot-magnon temperature at (0.5, 0.1, −0.5) (p. S9) lies outside the Fig. 3 data and is given without procedure, assumed dispersion, intensity-to-f(q) calibration or uncertainty.
state the momentum acceptance of each APD in r.l.u. along all three directions and show that points at |q| = 0.01–0.02 r.l.u. are not dominated by the resolution tail

notes: C13 ('amplitudes (a) must be capital A' in Fig. 3 caption) is already fixed in arXiv v1, which reads 'amplitudes (A)'. For C20, P18 challenges the same claim that the slow ~7 ns recovery stems from a magnon-phonon dispersion bottleneck, but proposes thermal diffusion rather than Kibble-Zurek defect coarsening as the alternative mechanism, so it is scored as 'partly'. For C12, P9 critiques the underdetermined separation of RXD decay and RDS rise where the signal is dominated by the negative RXD drop, but does not explicitly frame the upturn as simple recovery of the magnetic order.
